Fit a non-homogeneous Markov chain

Source: R/fittingFunctions.R
markovchainListFit.Rd

Estimates a non-homogeneous discrete time Markov chain, with one transition matrix for each pair of consecutive times, from a panel of trajectories observed at the same times.

Usage

markovchainListFit(data, byrow = TRUE, laplacian = 0, name)

Arguments

data

The trajectories: a matrix or data frame with one trajectory per row and one time per column (or the transpose, see byrow), or a list of trajectories (character vectors), possibly of different lengths.

byrow

Logical: for a matrix or data frame, is each trajectory a row (default) or a column?

laplacian

Laplace smoothing: a constant added to every transition count before normalizing (default 0).

name

Optional name of the fitted markovchainList.

Value

A list with element estimate, the fitted markovchainList; an empty list if no transition can be counted.

Details

The \(k\)-th transition matrix is the maximum likelihood estimate from the transitions observed between times \(k\) and \(k + 1\) (columns \(k\) and \(k + 1\), or positions \(k\) and \(k + 1\) of the trajectories long enough). Transitions with a missing value (NA) are ignored, and pairs of times without any complete transition are skipped.

See also

markovchainFit() for a homogeneous chain, rmarkovchain() to simulate from the fit.

Examples

data(holson)
# a homogeneous chain for the whole panel
singleMc <- markovchainFit(data = holson[, 2:12])
# one transition matrix for each pair of consecutive years
mclistFit <- markovchainListFit(data = holson[, 2:12], name = "holsonMcList")
mclistFit$estimate
